newsitem.title: HONG KONG: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - Philippine deals get done.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - Philippine deals get done.

text.p: The Philippines was in the news on Thursday with word that Manila had approved proposals by the World Bank and the International Finance Corp to issue Europeso bonds.
Details also were out on JG Summit's Eurobond.
The Philippines Monetary Board said it approved two proposals of the World Bank and the IFC, the World Bank's investment arm, to issue peso-denominated instruments offshore, known as Europeso notes.

"The launching of Europeso securities in international capital markets by these supranationals is expected to further stimulate investor interest in the country and attract foreign fund managers to take on the currency risk, given the issuers' AAA credit rating," Central Bank Governor Gabriel Singson said.

The issue size will be in the range of 2.5 to 4.0 billion pesos for each institution, the Central Bank said. The World Bank issue will be lead managed by Deutsche Morgan Grenfell and the IFC bond will be lead by Citibank.
Bankers have said that a Europeso issue will appeal mainly to Philippine investors.
In other news from the Philippines, JG Summit priced its seven-year US$200 million bond to yield 193 basis points over comparable Treasuries. ING Barings was the lead.

Syndicate managers said the bond looks like good value. The company's prior bond, a 5-1/2 year issue launched last October, has tightened in to about 150 basis points over Treasuries from 180 basis points at launch.
In other news, a unit of Hong Kong's China Resources launched a US$175 million floating rate note issue through arranger ING Barings.
The five-year notes pay a margin of 62 basis points over the London Interbank Offered Rate and an all-in return of 72 basis points.
